baseline_gap_evidence.gap_text: Cockpit renders recommendations; an explicit ordering/priority assertion end-to-end (highest-priority first, deterministic) is owed (ties to Wave-3/4 recommendation proofs).
baseline_gap_evidence.wave3_prior_proof_flaw: recommendation.integration.test.ts asserted ordering with lexical string compare (prev.priority >= curr.priority); all recs were 'high' (uniform) so mixed-priority ordering was never exercised

product_defects.description: orderBy [{priority:'desc'},{createdAt:'desc'}] on a plain String priority column sorts lexically (medium>low>high), rendering the owner's highest-priority recommendations LAST.
product_defects.fix: order by semantic priority rank (critical<high<medium<low) in-service, mirroring owner-dashboard.service.ts; stable sort preserves createdAt-desc tie-break. No schema/contract change.

product_defects.description: select requested non-existent columns expectedImpact/implementationPhase/executionCertaintyScore (Recommendation) and actions.priority (Action); prisma.recommendation.findMany threw PrismaClientValidationError on EVERY call, so the recommendations API route returned 500 unconditionally. Surfaced by the G2 proof (first maintained-lane caller).
product_defects.fix: expectedImpact -> estimatedImpact (real column); removed implementationPhase, executionCertaintyScore, actions.priority. No working consumer depended on them (endpoint always threw).

related_defect_out_of_scope.description: same invalid-select defect (expectedImpact/implementationPhase/executionCertaintyScore/scoreBreakdown). Distinct function not exercised by the G2 ordering proof; documented for a dedicated follow-up rather than shipped unproven in this gap PR.

proof_tests.lane: required maintained vitest suite (CI - Build & Test, TEST_WITH_DB=true)
assertions: six recs persisted in scrambled priority order (low,high,medium,high,low,medium) are returned engagement-scoped
priority rank monotonically non-decreasing (highest-priority-first) — fails under old lexical order, passes under fix
first returned is 'high', last is 'low'; both highs precede any medium, mediums precede any low
order is deterministic across repeated reads (same id + priority sequence)

validation_commands: caller audit: only recommendations API route + Wave-3 test (uniform 'high') + __ignored_tests__
npx vitest run src/services/__tests__/recommendation-priority-ordering.test.ts (delegated to PR CI)

wave3_test_impact: none — Wave-3 recs are all 'high' (uniform); stable sort preserves its createdAt-desc order; its assertions still hold
